- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to match mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 3–5 days to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is falling, model underestimates the drop; increase forecast downward by 1–3% to align with sentiment-driven volatility.
- Model consistently underestimates early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for first 5–7 days to capture sentiment lag.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “high-low-high” cycles, model tends to overfit recent highs; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to reduce false peaks.
- If true outcome is below 65 and forecast is above 70, model is overconfident; reduce forecast by 5–10% to reflect sentiment-driven risk aversion.
